links.outcome: SkinGPT-4 performance and fairness metrics across Fitzpatrick skin tones
links.effect: Average demographic parity 0.10 across Fitzpatrick types, with differences of 0.10-0.15 between lightest and darkest tones; weaker performance on darker tones.
links.quote: Large language models such as SkinGPT-4 showed weaker performance on darker tones.

links.outcome: Performance for underrepresented darker skin tones given lighter-tone-dominated training data
links.effect: Training dataset predominantly lighter skin tones; SkinGPT-4 weaker on darker tones, with 0.10-0.15 differences between lightest and darkest tones.
links.quote: Large language models such as SkinGPT-4 showed weaker performance on darker tones.

links.outcome: Fairness (demographic parity) and accuracy of finetuned models after bias mitigation across skin tones
links.effect: Custom models had average F1 0.75, precision 0.78, AUROC 0.78; average demographic parity 0.75, max disparity 0.21; best model parity 0.76-0.90 across Fitzpatrick I-VI.
links.quote: The best model achieved parity scores of 0.83, 0.83, 0.76, 0.89, 0.90, and 0.90 for Fitzpatrick I-VI, indicating robust fairness.

screen.reason: The study evaluates algorithmic bias, hallucinations, and fairness across skin tones in a vision-language model (SkinGPT-4) and tests model fine-tuning strategies with dermatologist evaluation on retrospective images, but does not test organizational deployment practices or safeguards.
